ra: Heavenly Father (Elohim) is the first member of the LDS Godhead (Articles of Faith 1).
Jehovah/Jesus Christ is the second member of the LDS Godhead (D&C 130:22).
The Holy Ghost is the third member of the LDS Godhead (D&C 130:22).
Heavenly Mother is the divine consort of Heavenly Father and co-parent of premortal spirits (Givens; Gospel Topics 'Mother in Heaven').
Jesus Christ is the Firstborn spirit child and literal Son of Heavenly Father in LDS theology (Givens).
As all premortal spirits are children of Heavenly Parents, Jesus is the firstborn spirit child of the Heavenly Mother as well (Givens).
Lucifer is a premortal spirit son of God who rebelled in the Council in Heaven (Book of Moses 4:1–4).
Lucifer offered a rival plan opposing Christ's at the Council in Heaven and was cast out (Book of Moses 4; D&C 76:25–28).
Under the Father, the premortal Jehovah/Christ is the creator of the worlds; Kolob governs in the LDS cosmological order created in this framework (Book of Abraham 3–4).
Heavenly Father presided over the premortal Council in Heaven where the plan of salvation was presented (Book of Abraham 3; Givens).
All premortal spirits are the spirit children of Heavenly Father (Book of Abraham 3; D&C 93:29; Givens).
Premortal spirits are co-parented by the Heavenly Mother (Givens; hymn 'O My Father').
The premortal spirits, including the 'noble and great ones,' participated in the Council in Heaven (Book of Abraham 3:22–28).
The Council in Heaven is the premortal episode within the overarching Plan of Salvation where that plan was presented (Givens).
Premortal spirit existence is the first stage of the LDS Plan of Salvation (Givens).
The three degrees of glory are the postmortal reward stage of the Plan of Salvation (D&C 76; Givens).
The Celestial Kingdom is the highest of the three degrees of glory (D&C 76).
The Terrestrial Kingdom is the middle of the three degrees of glory (D&C 76).
The Telestial Kingdom is the lowest of the three degrees of glory (D&C 76).
God dwells in the Celestial Kingdom, the highest degree of glory (D&C 76:62, 92).

Kolob is the great governing star 'nearest unto the throne of God,' i.e. the celestial body nearest God's dwelling (Book of Abraham 3:2–3, 9; Facsimile 2). [QA FIX: replaced invalid 'member_of Godhead' edge — Kolob is a realm, not a personage of the Godhead.]
Exaltation (godhood) is the culminating goal of the Plan of Salvation within the Celestial Kingdom (D&C 132; Givens).
Exaltation is attained only in the highest degree of the Celestial Kingdom (D&C 131:1–4).
Michael/Adam was among the noble and great premortal spirits before becoming the first man (D&C 107:54; Book of Abraham 3).

Moroni, as a resurrected human prophet, was (like all humans) a premortal spirit child of Heavenly Parents before mortal birth (Givens; Book of Abraham 3). [QA FIX: replaced stretched 'reveals Godhead' edge — Moroni revealed the golden plates, not 'the Godhead' as an object.]
The LDS Heavenly Father (Elohim) is the Restorationist reception/reconception of the Christian God the Father — embodied and exalted rather than the classical Trinity (Givens).
The LDS Jehovah/Jesus Christ is the Restorationist reception of the Christian Jesus, identifying him with the premortal Old Testament Jehovah (Bible Dictionary; Givens).
The LDS Holy Ghost is the Restorationist reception of the Christian Holy Spirit, reconceived as a distinct personage of spirit (D&C 130:22).
LDS doctrine receives the biblical Adam and identifies him with the archangel Michael (D&C 27:11; 107:54).
LDS scripture explicitly equates the archangel Michael with Adam (D&C 116; 107:54); links to the Christian archangel Michael as the equated figure.
